sentences.text:
Order 
Learned counsel for appellants/claimants requests for dispensing with service of respondent No.1.
2. On the basis of oral submission made by counsel for appellants and on own risk of appellants,
respondent Nos. 1 is dispensed with.

3. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act filed by the appellants/claimants arising out of the award dated 15.01.2010 passed by Ninth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Fastrack) (hereinafter referred as "Claims Tribunal), District- Gwalior in Claim Case No.315/2009 on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Ninth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Fastrack)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. The date of accident, negligence and issue of liability are not in dispute, however, the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:380 2 MA-546-2010 is not in question.

5. As per the findings of the Tribunal in the case of death of Mukesh Agarwal due to motor accident,
Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.4,92,500/- with interest from the date of filing of claim application till its realization to the claimants.

Smt.Asha vs Durga Prasad on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190965542/
1 6.
Counsel for appellants submitted that compensation as awarded by the Claims Tribunal by assessing the income of deceased to the tune of Rs.3,500/- per month is inadequate and is on lower side.
It is further submitted that deceased was unskilled labour, his income must be assessed as per Minimum Wages Act of unskilled labour at the time of alleged accident.

Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants contended that Claims Tribunal has committed error in not awarding future prospects and not awarding reasonable amount in other heads i.e. loss of estate, loss of consortium,
funeral expenses etc.
Hence, it is prayed that reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded to the claimants.

7. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.3/Insurance Company supported the impugned Award and submitted that the Claims Tribunal has rightly assessed the compensation on the basis of the evidence available on record.
It is contended that the appeal lacks merit and deserves to be dismissed.

8. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
9 .
After hearing counsel for the parties, it is found that Claims Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased is on lower side.

In considered opinion of this Court, the just and proper amount of the income of the deceased as per Minimum Wages Act in the present case is Rs.3,575/-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:380 3 MA-546-2010 per month of an unskilled labour instead of Rs.3,500/- per month which has wrongly been assessed by the Claims Tribunal. .

10. As regard to loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700 , the claimant is entitled for loss of income including future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Pranay Sethi (supra), future prospects be added at 40%.

Further,
as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, even if age of the claimant is to be taken into account, Claims Tribunal has rightly applied multiplier of 15.
11.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the appellant/claimant is entitled to receive compensation under the following heads:
 HEAD   Income Rs.3575 X   Future Prospects@40% Rs.60,060/
 Dependency 3/4 Rs.45,045/
 Multiplier 15 Rs.6,75,67

Other Heads:-
 Loss of Consortium Rs.40,000  Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,000/-

Total Compensation = Rs.9,05,675/-
Smt.Asha vs Durga Prasad on 6 January, 2026

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190965542/
2 12.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation payable in the present case comes to Rs.Rs.9,05,675/- as against the sum of Rs.4,92,500/- awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.

Accordingly, the appellant/claimant is held entitled to an additional compensation of Rs.4,13,175/-
over and above the amount already awarded by the Tribunal.

13. Consequently, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, and the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:380 4 MA-546-2010 compensation amount is enhanced by Rs.4,13,175/-.
The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
It is made clear that appellants/claimants are not entitled to get interest from 21.07.2015 to 05.01.2024.
The enhanced amount shall be paid to the appellants/claimants within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order.
The remaining conditions imposed by the learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

14. In case the enhanced compensation exceeds the valuation of the appeal, the appellants shall deposit the differential Court fee (if not already paid) within a period of one month from today and furnish proof of such payment before the Registry.
Upon compliance, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of this order.
15. In view of the foregoing discussion, the miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellants stands disposed of accordingly.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *VJ*
